newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Bullishness seen in Hilton/ITT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Bullishness seen in Hilton/ITT.

text.p: Options on Hilton Hotels Corp and ITT Corp were fairly busy Tuesday as both stocks rallied after Hilton offered late Monday to buy ITT for $55 a share.
Traders in both pits said investors were not focusing on any one strike, exercise month or strategy, but that in general the activity suggested they were viewing the proposed buyout favorably.
"It looks like the market likes the idea," said one trader at the Pacific Stock Exchange, where Hilton options trade. ITT options trade at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
"There hasn't been one series that they've been buying or selling," the trader said, referring to Hilton options. "It's been two-sided paper."
Hilton shares were up 3-3/4 at 28-1/2 at about 1045 CST/1645 GMT after reaching a session high of 30 in consolidated trading. Volume topped 3.7 million shares.
ITT, which rallied to 58-1/2 in after-hours trading Monday, was down 3/4 at 57-3/4 in consolidated trading on volume of about 7.4 million.
But on the New York Stock Exchange, the stock was up 15-1/8 to 57-3/4.
Volatilities on Hilton options were fairly steady in the low 30 region but volatilities on ITT climbed to around 30. In December, ITT option volatilities were around 18.
"I think we're getting some interest from arb guys doing ITT," the trader at the Pacific Stock Exchange said. "I think if they're buying ITT, they're hedging themselves with Hilton options."
The Hilton February 25 call was the most active option in the group, with volume of about 1,360 contracts.
The Hilton February 30 call traded nearly 800 contracts and the April 30 call traded about 735.
Among Hilton puts, the April 32-1/2 was most active, with volume of 575 contracts. Other actives included the February 25, 27-1/2 and 30 calls.
The trader said orders were coming from both institutional and retail investors.
"Word travels fast these days," he said.
A broker in Chicago said he had sold some ITT calls for a client looking to take profits as the call premiums surged along with the stock.
The most active ITT call was the March 60, which traded about 6,135 contracts. It rose 1-3/8 to 1-7/16.
The March 55 call, which gained 4-1/8 to 4-1/4, traded nearly 4,100 contracts, making second most active.
The busiest ITT put was the March 55, with turnover of 955 contracts.
"It's crazy," a trader at the CBOE said of ITT options.
He said it appeared a sizable number of investors were trying to sell out-of-the-money premium in back month options to take advantage of volatility.
But he added that volatilities would likely drop once the stock settles down. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
